analysis.title: Mutual Fundamentals: Mutual funds remain selective within the AI complex
key_insights: Goldman's Q3 2026 survey covers 453 large-cap active mutual funds with $3.9 trillion in equity assets. 42% are beating their benchmarks YTD versus a 37% historical average.

81% of large-cap growth funds are beating their benchmarks, the highest share in over a decade. Only 4% of large-cap value funds are, the lowest share on record in the report's comparison. Value funds have the best absolute YTD return (+14.4%) but trail a Russell 1000 Value benchmark up 23.1%.
Mutual fund cash is 1.1% of assets at the end of September, matching the December 2025 low. It rose briefly around the start of the US-Iran war and then fell back.

Active US equity mutual funds have seen about $350B of outflows YTD and are on track for a 12th straight year of outflows. US equity ETFs have taken in about $960B YTD and about $210B since the start of Q4.

Mutual funds were underweight AI-exposed equities ahead of the AI complex's weakness since the start of Q4. Excluding mega-caps, AI stocks were 12% of the average fund at the start of Q4, a 130 bp underweight, narrowed by about 44 bp from Q2. Including mega-caps, AI exposure averages 34% against a 40% benchmark weight.

Funds added to select AI pockets in Q3 despite the underweight. The most popular increases were AMD, PLTR, SNDK, SNOW, WDC, TWLO, PANW and CRWD. The most popular decreases among AI-linked names were AMAT, LRCX, CSCO and KLAC.

The average large-cap fund was 722 bp underweight the Magnificent 7 at the end of Q3, effectively unchanged on the quarter. Part of the gap comes from diversification restrictions. Growth funds are 1,002 bp underweight, core 731 bp, value 434 bp.

The average fund is underweight every Mag 7 name except AMZN, which is an average overweight for the first time since 2016. Only AAPL and AMZN have beaten the equal-weight S&P 500 YTD, and four of the seven have negative YTD returns.
A majority of funds cut shares in every Mag 7 name except MSFT in Q3. The biggest net reductions were GOOGL (net -127 funds) and AAPL (net -71).

High return dispersion and improved market breadth have supported mutual fund returns. Breadth has improved through a catch-up from laggards and a modest catch-down from the largest stocks, and dispersion stays high because higher stock volatility offset higher correlations.

Funds were relatively well positioned for Q4 volatility. Among the top 15 best and worst S&P 500 performers QTD, the average fund was slightly overweight the median best performer and 3 bp underweight the median worst performer.

The average fund is most overweight Industrials (+200 bp), Health Care (+199 bp, a 10-year high) and Financials (+196 bp). It is most underweight Info Tech (-631 bp). Industrials, Health Care, Energy and Staples tilts sit at or above the 95th percentile of the past 10 years, while Comm Services and Info Tech tilts sit at the 3rd percentile.

Financials had the largest tilt cut in Q3 (-35 bp), led by Banks (-22 bp). JPM, BAC and C were among the 20 most popular decreases. Info Tech had the largest increase (+29 bp), broad-based and led by Software and Semiconductors.

Goldman attributes the Health Care overweight partly to the sector's inverse correlation with the AI trade. Life Sciences Tools is now the second most overweight industry in the sector behind Health Care Providers. RVTY, ILMN and TMO were among the most popular Q3 increases.
Funds across all styles trimmed tilts to Consumer Staples and Utilities in Q3.

Since the start of Q4 the mutual fund overweight basket GSTHMFOW is up 5%, ahead of the equal-weight S&P 500 (+3%) and the underweight basket GSTHMFUW (-7%). YTD the overweights have lagged the underweights (8% versus 16%). Goldman rebalanced the baskets: 13 new names in GSTHMFOW, including GILD, CRM and NET, and 7 new names in GSTHMFUW, including NFLX, CSCO and PFE.

The largest overweights by style are MA, V and DHR in core, AMZN, TMO and STX in growth, and GOOGL, NVDA and TXN in value. The largest underweights are AAPL, NVDA and TSLA in core, NVDA, GOOGL and AAPL in growth, and AAPL, AMZN and BRK.B in value.

sector_views.rationale: Average large-cap fund tilt of +200 bp, the largest overweight, at or above the 95th percentile of the past 10 years. This is fund positioning, not a Goldman recommendation.
Average fund tilt of +199 bp, a 10-year high, helped by the sector's inverse correlation with the AI trade. Life Sciences Tools is the main source of added exposure.
Average fund tilt of +196 bp, but cut by 35 bp in Q3, the largest reduction of any sector, led by Banks.
Average fund tilt of -631 bp, at the 3rd percentile of the past 10 years. Funds raised the tilt by 29 bp in Q3, led by Software and Semiconductors.
Average fund tilt of -64 bp, at the 3rd percentile of the past 10 years.
Average fund tilt of +2 bp after a 14 bp cut in Q3. Funds across styles trimmed Staples and Utilities.

risk_factors: Continued weakness in the AI complex, which has struggled since the start of Q4, hits the stocks funds added in Q3 (AMD, PLTR, SNDK, WDC, STX).
A narrowing of market breadth would remove a driver of mutual fund excess returns.
Value funds struggle to match a fast-rising Russell 1000 Value benchmark, with only 4% outperforming.
